Split button

A main action joined to a menu button that holds other ways to do the same thing.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • When one action is right most of the time and two or more close alternatives are needed now and then, such as Start task and Start on a new branch.
  • When the alternatives are variations of the main action, so the reader would look for them beside it.

When not to use it

  • For actions that are not variations of one another. Use buttons, or a menu behind a button that names what they act on.
  • For a single alternative. Show it as a second button.
  • To choose a value that stays chosen. Use a select or a segmented control.
  • For an option that is on or off. Use a toggle button.

Variants

secondary
The default. Both halves are plain buttons.
primary
The main action also carries gw-button--primary when it is the one main action of the view. The menu button stays a plain button, so the pair never shows two accent fills.

Sizes

default
44px tall. The menu button is 44px wide.

Accessibility

  • Use a div with gw-split-button, role="group" and an aria-label that names the main action. It holds the main action, then the menu button, then the menu, in that order.
  • The main action is a button with gw-button and gw-split-button__action. Its label is a verb and what it acts on. Pressing it never opens the menu.
  • The menu button is a button with gw-button and gw-split-button__toggle, popovertarget set to the menu's id and aria-haspopup="menu". It holds the chevron icon with aria-hidden="true" and its own name in a gw-visually-hidden span, such as More ways to start the task. The name is never the main action's label again.
  • The menu is the menu component, copied from its examples, with the same name as the menu button in its aria-label. Its items are other ways to do the main action. The main action itself is not repeated in it.
  • At most the main action is primary. Two primary halves fail the one-primary-action rule.
  • Tab reaches the main action and then the menu button. Enter and Space activate each. The browser opens and closes the menu, closes it on Escape and on a press outside, and returns focus to the menu button. Arrow keys inside the menu are the menu component's.
  • When the action is unavailable, set disabled on both halves. While the main action runs, set aria-busy="true" on it, change its label to say what is happening, and set disabled on the menu button.
  • The component needs no script of its own.

Classes

  • gw-split-button
  • gw-split-button__action
  • gw-split-button__toggle
